## Wine, ancient landscapes, whales and Welsh culture

From Mendoza, continue to San Juan and on to Ischigualasto and Talampaya national parks. The urban setting gives way to desert, canyons and rock formations that hold fossils of animals and plants hundreds of millions of years old.

The final part of the trip takes you to the Atlantic. In Puerto Madryn, visit the Valdés Peninsula, go looking for southern right whales, see a colony of Magellanic penguins and travel to Gaiman, a town founded by Welsh settlers. The route links the capital, wine country, desert parks and the Atlantic coast.

The scenery and focus keep changing over the 13 days. You’ll see urban Argentina, the high Andes, wine country, landscapes shaped by geological time and the wildlife of the Atlantic. Even the longer journeys take you between distinctly different parts of the country, with each leg bringing a new side of Argentina into view.
